scientific_claim_freeze.robust_label_rule: Use robust only when the reported direction or mechanism is preserved across the applicable core envelope. Report upper-stress results separately and never use them to establish robustness.
scientific_claim_freeze.prohibited_inference: A count across the illustrative 15 trajectories is not a test of robustness to lower or replacement data-center paths.

interpretation_boundaries: All load paths are named scenarios; none is labelled a central or probabilistic forecast.
LBNL reports annual energy. Energy-to-average-power conversion is arithmetic, while peak-equivalent planning load is a separately audited mapping.
The LBNL 50 percent utilization illustration for interconnection capacity is not used as a planning-peak conversion.
Values after 2030 are explicit continuation scenarios and are not attributed to LBNL.
Generic national paths are not automatically additional to official regional demand forecasts; embedded-load overlap is retained as a full envelope.
The national increment is not automatically assigned in full to the seven-region siting footprint; footprint capture is an explicit evidence-based sensitivity.
MISO and ERCOT source-identified load-path replacement with linked-response bounds governs attribution for those regions.
PJM is limited to strict-floor partial identification; SPP, NYISO and ISO-NE generic rows are additional-load stresses rather than complete source-path replacements.
The peak-equivalent mapping is a traceable load-shape scenario family, not seven-region empirical validation.
Robust regional labels require stability across the applicable core envelope; upper stresses are reported separately.
A negative balance means resources fall below the region-native reference requirement under the stated scenario, not that outages are predicted.
Region-native GW balances are not summed across planning regions.

generation_scale_exclusion.reason: Issuer identifies private generation, not equivalent data-center electrical demand
